name: Von Willebrand Disease Type 2M

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ISTH-SSC Diagnostic Criteria for Von Willebrand Disease

criteria.description: Identification of a heterozygous mutation in the VWF gene affecting platelet binding without significant loss of multimeric structure
Reduced von Willebrand factor activity to antigen ratio (VWF:RCo/VWF:Ag) typically below 0.7
Normal or near-normal VWF multimeric pattern on electrophoresis
Personal or family history of mucocutaneous bleeding symptoms consistent with a bleeding disorder

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic VWF gene mutation plus reduced VWF activity to antigen ratio with normal multimeric pattern
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other VWD subtypes and platelet function disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mucocutaneous bleeding with normal VWF multimer pattern
searchTerms: bleeding from mucous membranes with normal clotting factors
mucosal bleeding despite normal VWF pattern
easy bleeding with normal von Willebrand factor

pathognomonic.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding time despite normal platelet count
searchTerms: bleeding lasts long even with normal platelets
prolonged bleeding time despite normal platelet levels
extended bleeding despite normal platelet count

occasional.symptomName: Postoperative bleeding disproportionate to surgical trauma

occasional.notes: Less common than in other bleeding disorders

laboratory: Reduced VWF ristocetin cofactor activity to antigen ratio (<0.7)
Normal platelet count with prolonged bleeding time
Normal or mildly reduced factor VIII levels
imaging: Imaging generally not diagnostic but may be used to assess bleeding complications such as hemarthrosis or intracranial hemorrhage
other: Normal platelet aggregation studies except for ristocetin-induced platelet aggregation abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Loss of high molecular weight VWF multimers
More severe reduction in VWF activity
Defect in platelet GPIb receptor rather than VWF

redFlags: Severe mucocutaneous bleeding disproportionate to trauma
Postpartum hemorrhage requiring transfusion or intervention
references: Sadler JE. Von Willebrand disease type 2M: a qualitative defect in platelet binding. Blood. 1998.
Federici AB et al. Diagnosis and classification of von Willebrand disease: a consensus report. J Thromb Haemost. 2008.
Orphanet: Von Willebrand disease type 2M. ORPHA:166090.
